# HotStuff Chained Pacemaker with Locked-Node Safety

## Root-cause analysis

Unsafe behavior in this problem class comes from several interacting missing invariants:

1. **Unverified high QCs** — accepting a proposal whose carried QC is fake, sub-quorum, or for a different block.
2. **Votes that ignore the lock** — allowing a replica to vote on a branch that does not extend `lockedHash`, especially when the proposal’s high QC is not applied before voting.
3. **A non-HotStuff commit rule** — committing a block after one QC instead of the chained 3-chain rule.
4. **Loss of durable state across crashes** — losing `lastVoted`, `lockedQC`, `highQC`, or the committed tip enables double-voting or unlocking.
5. **A non-replayable harness** — randomized scheduling without a recorded event log cannot prove safety.

The fix is an explicit invariant-preserving protocol plus an event-sourced checker:

- one vote per view, persisted before sending;
- a vote requires a valid high QC and extension of the locked branch;
- applying the proposal’s parent QC as a lock barrier before voting;
- committing the ancestor at `QC.Height - 2`;
- view changes driven by a verified aggregate view-change certificate;
- deterministic simulation with reordering, phase crashes, persistence, and equivocation;
- exhaustive log replay checking same-height uniqueness and monotone committed prefixes.

## Exact fix

Complete source and write-up are in:

```text
~/hotstuff-solution/
├── go.mod
├── types.go
├── replica.go
├── world.go
├── checker.go
├── hotstuff_test.go
├── cmd/hotstuff-demo/main.go
└── SOLUTION.md
```

Run:

```bash
cd ~/hotstuff-solution
go test ./...
go vet ./...
go run ./cmd/hotstuff-demo -seed 42 -views 20 -crashes 1 \
  -equivocate -equivocate-first 2
```

Critical vote rule:

```go
if err := r.W.verifyBlock(b); err != nil {
    reject
}
if b.ParentQC != nil {
    r.onQC(b.ParentQC) // apply carried high QC as a lock barrier
}
if !r.extendsLock(b.Hash) {
    reject
}
if !r.LockedHash.IsZero() &&
   (b.ParentQC == nil || b.ParentQC.BlockHeight < r.LockedHeight) {
    reject
}
if prev, ok := r.LastVoted[r.View]; ok && prev != b.Hash {
    reject
}
r.LastVoted[b.View] = b.Hash
r.save() // persist before sending the vote
```

The single certificate gate used by both prepare QCs and view-change certificates:

```go
func VerifyCertificate(c *Certificate, n, f int, pub []ed25519.PublicKey) error
```

It checks distinct signers, one valid Ed25519 signature per signer, at least `n-f` signers, embedded high-QC validity, and that the selected view-change high QC is the maximum present in the votes.

Chained commit rule:

```go
if haveBlock && block.Height >= 3 {
    r.commitAncestor(block, block.Height-2, c)
}
```

`CheckLog` replays every certificate-bearing record and every commit, checking:

- valid 3-chain justification;
- no different block committed at the same height;
- parent linkage to already-committed heights;
- no replica commits decreasing heights;
- every new commit extends that replica’s committed prefix.

`MinimizeViolation` delta-debugs the recorded trace and prints the smallest failing suffix/prefix.

## Verification

Executed with Go 1.26:

```text
$ go test -count=1 -v ./...
=== RUN   TestStableProgressAndSafety
--- PASS: TestStableProgressAndSafety (0.10s)
=== RUN   TestChaosEquivocationCrashSafety
--- PASS: TestChaosEquivocationCrashSafety (5.80s)
=== RUN   TestViewChangeCertificateDrivesProposal
--- PASS: TestViewChangeCertificateDrivesProposal (0.07s)
=== RUN   TestPrepareCertificateVerification
--- PASS: TestPrepareCertificateVerification (0.00s)
=== RUN   TestCheckerFindsAndMinimizesCounterexample
    minimal counterexample:
        conflicting commits at the same height: height 1 has cc161e220e079e7f and 31b82c3be80dd32d
          t=3 replica=0 commit height=1 hash=cc161e220e079e7f parent=3dd645c35eaa6454
          t=5 replica=1 commit height=1 hash=31b82c3be80dd32d parent=3dd645c35eaa6454
--- PASS: TestCheckerFindsAndMinimizesCounterexample (0.00s)
=== RUN   TestHarnessIsDeterministic
--- PASS: TestHarnessIsDeterministic (0.33s)
PASS
```

Representative harness runs:

```text
$ go run ./cmd/hotstuff-demo -seed 7 -views 10 -crashes 0 -equivocate -equivocate-first 1
seed=7 views=10 commits=28 maxHeight=7 fast=9 viewChange=1 equivocations=1
replay checker: OK (no conflicting same-height commits; committed prefixes are monotone)

$ go run ./cmd/hotstuff-demo -seed 42 -views 20 -crashes 1 -equivocate -equivocate-first 2
seed=42 views=20 commits=60 maxHeight=15 fast=19 viewChange=2 equivocations=2
replay checker: OK (no conflicting same-height commits; committed prefixes are monotone)
```

An extended mixed `n=4` / `n=7` probe completed 6,765 commits with 631 view-change-certificate proposals and no replay violations. The synthetic conflicting-commit test confirms the checker detects real violations and minimizes them to the two-commit trace shown above.

signatures.description: Implement a HotStuff-style BFT consensus core in Go with a chained pacemaker and explicit safety reasoning: a replica votes for a proposal only if it extends its locked branch and carries a valid highQC, and a view change is driven by a generic prepare certificate whose aggregated signature the new leader must verify before proposing. Include a deterministic in-process simulation harness that injects arbitrary message reordering, phase-to-phase replica crashes with recovery from persisted state, and equivocating leaders, then prove by exhaustive replay of the recorded message log that no two conflicting blocks ever commit in the same height and that the committed prefix is monotone. Provide the safety-invariant checker and a minimal counterexample trace for any violation the harness detects.
